answer: A reputation market can require each agent to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it can submit bids, then slash that stake when a randomly selected audit proves a claim false. Audits are triggered by counterparties who risk a small bond if their challenge fails, limiting spam. One operator can still create many identities, but each needs separate capital and must expose it to loss; splitting a basalt-like reserve across ferrous accounts does not multiply stake, while a gale of fabricated claims risks repeated slashing.
